description: Buscamos los mejor para el equipo
summary: "The Disciples of Adriel" addresses the challenge of NASA's abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars. We developed an educational and interactive narrative platform to introduce school-aged space enthusiasts to the hardware and science of these historic missions. We tackled this topic by combining open science data from NASA and AI tools to translate complex technical concepts into a clear and user-friendly format, designing original visuals without altering the agency's official logos. This is of great importance as it connects complex space data with young minds, transforming distant machinery into inspiring educational milestones that cultivate future STEM generations.
details:
What exactly does it do?

It is a narrative and interactive platform that compiles and explains the history of the hardware that NASA has left on the Moon, Mars and deep space since the 1960s (such as rovers, scientific instruments and probes).

How does it work?

Present the information in a guided and friendly way so that students can explore each mission, understand the purpose of the space equipment and know their current state through interactive cards or a visual narrative journey.

Benefits you have

Accessible education: Translate complex scientific and technical data into a clear, exciting and perfectly adapted language for school-age children and young people.

Promotion of scientific vocations: Arouses curiosity about science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) using real examples of space exploration.

Valorization of the space heritage: It teaches that the "finished" missions are not forgotten, but are the basis of all the knowledge we have today of the solar system.

Expected impact

Generational inspiration: Impact school-age students so that they see space exploration not as something distant, but as a possible future where they themselves could design the following missions to other worlds.

Effective disclosure: Create public awareness about the history of space technology in a dynamic way that can be easily integrated into schools or communities of space enthusiasts.


Tools, programming languages, hardware or software used

Data and Sources: Open data and official NASA scientific information on space missions.

Artificial Intelligence and Writing: AI tools to synthesize, structure and adapt the technical narrative to a didactic and children's format.

Development and Design: Digital creation platforms, web design or interactive interfaces (e.g. HTML/CSS/JS, React, Canva, Genially, Figma or other prototyping tools used by the team).

How creative is the project?

Original narrative approach ("Abandoned but not forgotten"): Instead of seeing the inactive hardware on the Moon or Mars as space junk, the project transforms it into the "protagonists" of a story of exploration and

Independent visual design: The rules of the challenge were strictly respected when creating their own and original visual elements, without modifying or using logos, flags or official brand identities of NASA.

What factors were considered in the team?

Target audience (School age): The level of complexity of language was carefully evaluated, ensuring that the technical terms of space science were easy to digest and attractive to children and young people.

Scientific rigor: It was validated that the historical information on the missions, rovers and probes was true based on the available official data.

Collaboration and roles: The combination of team skills (data research, narrative writing, visual design and technological structuring) was considered to meet the challenge deliverables on time.
